newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BRUSSELS BOURSE POISED FOR FRESH PROGRESS.
newsitem.headline: BRUSSELS BOURSE POISED FOR FRESH PROGRESS.

text.p: Belgian shares look set to rise further on Wednesday, dealers said, likely to draw more support from a firming dollar and steady to better bond prices.

The bourse would continue to advance on the perception that key German interest rates were on hold for at least another week, while the chances of the Federal Reserve raising U.S. rates were not rated very high.

Dealers said the view that leading interest rates would be left unchanged for next month or two could help the bourse find its way back to the record levels it abandoned some two weeks ago. The Bel-20 index .BFX peaked at 2,621.90 on July 28.

The index gained more than 30 points to end at 2,451.95 on Tuesday, helped by the Bundesbank's decision to leave its repo rate unchanged DE-CEN, propelling the dollar DEM= and supporting export-oriented stocks.
"There are still many buyers out there, ready to jump in on the slightest positive news report," a trader said.

Although some predicted caution before Wednesday's releases of U.S. PPIs and retail sales data US-MCE, the trader said the chance was small the Fed would respond with a rate hike to the numbers. PPIs are forecast to show muted inflation, while retail sales are seen showing some strength.
